title: The Amount a Premium Return Is Worked Out On
content:
The amount the return of premium on a given-up Pass and Trip Protection plan is worked out on is taken from
the plan's own premium and from the payments matched to premium entries on its protection account.

| The records show | The amount the return is worked out on |
| --- | --- |
| The premium frozen on the plan standing above the payments matched to premium entries, and the plan's premium collected alongside the covered holding's instalments | The premium frozen on the plan |
| The protection account carrying no payment matched to a premium entry | Nothing |
| Any other case | The total of the payments matched to premium entries |

**Reading the schedule.** The rows are read in the order given, and the first is compound: the premium frozen
on the plan must stand above the total of the payments matched to premium entries, and the plan must at the
same time be one whose premium is collected alongside the covered holding's instalments. A plan collected in a
single payment never falls on the first row, however much of its premium stands uncollected.

**Worked cases (hypothetical inputs).** A plan riding on the covered holding's instalments with 349.00 USD of
premium frozen on it and 120.00 USD matched to premium entries: the amount the return is worked out on is
349.00 USD. A plan collected in a single payment with the same figures: the amount is the 120.00 USD matched.
A plan of either kind with nothing at all matched to a premium entry: the amount is nothing, and the return
worked out on it is nothing whatever the rest of the working gives.
